edge.rationale: Using symbols for missing values depends on interpreting equality as a relation between two equivalent expressions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats a box or letter as an operation cue rather than as a value placeholder in a balanced statement.

edge.rationale: Using inverse operations to isolate an unknown depends on understanding symbols as placeholders for values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies inverse operations mechanically without recognising which symbol is being solved for.

edge.rationale: Two-step equations extend inverse-operation reasoning across more than one undoing step.
edge.failure_signal: Learner performs only one inverse operation and stops before isolating the variable.

edge.rationale: Solving linear inequalities uses inverse-operation equation reasoning plus inequality-specific order rules.
edge.failure_signal: Learner solves the boundary equation but cannot preserve or interpret the inequality solution set.

edge.rationale: Graphical solution of simultaneous linear equations requires graphing linear rules and interpreting their lines.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot graph two linear equations accurately enough to identify their intersection.

edge.rationale: Prior experience solving simultaneous equations supports later matrix methods without making the broad matrix-operations unit a diagnostic learner-state dependency.
